# V78 DEV1 implementation and acceptance

The Web baseline is V77.2.1-STABLE at `7046e533ec9d01a8ca520068d7b5cfb092d1ccc2`. The Android integration reference is V10.2 candidate `095f4e55815ea0ca4a9d8f9d9ee2192833ec088e`. Android main resolved to V9-STABLE at `8bc45f3e0b034fd94a5ac7142afde936726cec26`. Implementation uses WEB-001, WEB-002 and WEB-014 from the completed Web audit and AND-001 through AND-003 from the attached Android audit. The V78 branch and draft are for DEV1 acceptance. Production remains on the pinned Web stable release.

| Finding | Disposition | Implementation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| WEB-001 | Fixed in shared Web storage | Team, plan and link mutations use a single same-origin IndexedDB writer lane and expected per-entity revisions. Unrelated changes merge. A stale edit to the same entity is rejected with a recoverable draft. |
| WEB-002 | Fixed in the shared Web renderer | A validated observation watermark is separate from the displayed save. Newer equivalent observations advance only ordering metadata. Equal sequence with changed bytes reports a conflict. Manual imports may show older actual data. |
| AND-001 | Fixed in the shared Web renderer | Full raw validation and fingerprinting precede manual supersession. An invalid full-size import and a forged parsed hint cannot cancel linked hydration. The pinned native bundle still needs DEV8 integration. |
| WEB-014 | Fixed for the existing team import path | Legacy bare, v1 and v2 JSON validate before any team or plan write. Nested fields, bounded data, resource URLs and references are checked. Team and plan commit together. |
| AND-002 / AND-003 | Shared Web contract only | Native inspection, explicit deletion/unlink, generation-scoped pending/confirmed replacement and restart/cancellation receipts. Java, grant retention/release and old adapter behavior remain DEV8 deliverables. |

## Storage, migration and conflicts

`dev1-storage.js` owns the canonical `takdex-v78-state-v1` envelope. Teams, plans and link intent are separate tables with per-entity revisions and tombstones. One IndexedDB **readwrite** transaction serializes the synchronous canonical compare, edit and localStorage write across documents. The commit point is the successful canonical `setItem`, with no await between comparison and publication. If it fails, the preceding envelope remains authoritative. Import and deletion update both team and plan inside that one write. Deletion also records explicit link intent. Plan saves verify the referenced team still exists in the selected game. Retained historical plans from older releases remain readable. New IDs use UUIDs where available.

Migration is lazy on the first successful mutation. Existing data comes from `poketact-teams` and `takdex-v74-playthrough-plans`. V78 reads the canonical envelope once present. The legacy keys remain as compatibility projections for older readers, including the old native adapter. A projection error is shown separately from a failed canonical write. Interruption or quota between projections cannot split the V78 team and plan. The next successful canonical write attempts projection again. Copies take additional origin quota. Pre-V78 documents cannot join the lane, and an older runtime editing the projection during a mixed-version window is unsupported. Reload tabs after upgrading. A failed or unavailable IndexedDB writer disables mutations, preserves readable data and offers the normal exports. There is no unlocked fallback. Chromium was tested. Other WebView and browser implementations need their own validation.

On same-entity conflict the durable winner stays in storage. The losing tab shows an alert with a downloadable copy of the pending edit, then the user can reload and reapply it. The recovery JSON is an inspection artifact. Normal portable team sharing still uses the v1/v2-compatible import/export format. Unsaved conflict copies are held by the document, so download before reloading. Legacy corruption leaves the raw data untouched and provides a recovery export with all three keys. Corrupt or inaccessible state is fail-closed for mutations and native grant release.

`dev1-import.js` validates the complete payload before writing, retains safe unknown nested legacy fields, and preserves the existing nickname and display-name length limits. It accepts identity-only historical fields and warns for an absent fulfilled Pokémon without inventing its association. It rejects duplicate actual PIDs and duplicate fulfilled claims. Same species with different PIDs are accepted. A portable import gets a fresh team ID and retains plan content, while save-source generations and grants remain local. Resource URLs must use HTTPS without credentials. `app.js` routes user edits, background enrichment and legacy battle-profile migration through the writer. `maps.js` obtains its default team context through the authoritative reader.

## Synchronization policy

`save-sync.js` parses the raw 512 KiB input with the existing Gen V checksum and bank validator. The supported adapter can still send `linked`, `parsed` and `relink`; a supplied parsed object is a hint without authority. A SHA-256 fingerprint binds the verified bytes for equal-sequence and staged relink checks. Sequence arithmetic uses the unsigned 16-bit ring and treats the half-ring boundary as stale. Linked order is scoped to team, game, trainer and source generation. Provider modification time is retained as metadata. A changed trainer requires explicit replacement. Legacy native checkpoints with a proven native checkpoint field can seed the first watermark. An old generic display snapshot has no reliable manual/automatic provenance, so its first linked observation establishes the watermark.

An equivalent observation changes only link state. No team-saved, progression or save-synced events fire for that observation. A manual historical display leaves the linked watermark intact. Later equivalent observations leave that deliberate display alone. A later meaningful linked change may apply. Progression-only meaningful updates emit progression and team events without a party event.

In one renderer, a newer validated manual intent suppresses older hydration. Invalid input never claims that intent. Linked reads can hydrate in parallel and resolve by the durable sequence at commit. A pending replacement leaves the old source usable. The atomic generation change prevents earlier reads from publishing after the replacement. While hydration is pending, deletion, a game/source change, an intervening manual commit or a builder revision blocks stale publication. Cross-document manual or replacement commits use the same transaction boundary and guard the observed revisions. A conflict can be retried explicitly. A completed sync targets its team ID and preserves other teams' drafts and planner UI. The cartridge save remains read-only.

## Private acceptance checklist

- Open two tabs. Create different teams, edit different teams and set different deadlines. Reload and verify all choices. In two tabs edit one team or plan. Verify one wins, the other shows a recovery alert, and download works.
- In a test Black 2 team, import/synchronize compatible saves. Check that an acquired replacement follows its identity through evolution, reordering and absence, while selected stages, locks, moves and deadlines remain unchanged. Use the normal editor to check Actual versus Planned Gym coverage.
- At a mobile width, open Move Checker from a planned move and return. Verify the same slot, open editor, query and scroll. Confirm the conflict message fits the screen.
- Export and import a test team. Verify the moves and plan round trip and that an invalid file leaves the team list unchanged. Verify offline boot, saved teams, plans and pack state after updating from stable.

For native recovery and grant handling, see [DEV8 handoff](DEV8-HANDOFF.md). Native implementation, physical Samsung testing and APK packaging are outside this candidate.

## Verification evidence

- `TAKDEX_REFERENCE_SAVES=/workspace/work/retail-saves node --test .github/v76/*.test.cjs .github/v77/*.test.cjs .github/v78/*.test.cjs` exercises four reference saves, the parser, progression, battle, acquisition, legacy ownership, and bounded imports. Local evidence used copied fixture saves and no user data.
- `node .github/v78/dev1-browser.cjs http://127.0.0.1:8894/` uses Chromium and checksum-valid synthetic Black 2 saves. Suites can be selected with `TAKDEX_FOCUS=storage|sync|recovery`. The storage suite covers concurrent same-origin team and plan operations, conflicts, draft download and deletion. Sync covers 10/12/11 ordering, wrap, equal/stale conflicts, timestamp and trainer handling, manual display, progression, malformed overlap, reverse hydration, team switch, builder conflict, deletion and relink. Recovery covers unsupported writer, absent/corrupt/inaccessible store, older-file prepare and retry, cancellation, relink/import quota failure, interrupted compatibility projection, restart and file-size/nested validation.
- Existing ownership verification covers both 360 and 412 CSS px, caught replacement and actual-vs-planned Gym readiness, same-PID evolution, absence/return, reorder, independent plan state, ambiguity and restart. Team management covers legacy migration, stats, items, ability and JSON export/import. Move Checker return retains selected slot, open editor, search and scroll. The same-origin service-worker upgrade preserves offline boot, teams, plans and cached pack fixture storage.
- Earlier smoke attempts exposed asynchronous test assumptions. Plan checks now wait for persistence. The delayed encounter probe only pauses the save hydration call, so map and other reference readers stay independent. The stale-tab conflict scenario refreshes the second tab before starting the intentional edit during hydration.
